column3: The Hebrew calls David “a son of death”; BSB renders this image as “he must surely die.”
The Hebrew explicitly says Jonathan answered his father Saul; BSB leaves the addressee implicit.
The Hebrew does not name Jonathan as the one the spear was aimed at and uses a verb for striking him; the BSB supplies Jonathan and says “to kill him.”
The Hebrew calls what he did not eat “bread”; BSB uses “any food.” It gives his grief over David and his father’s shaming as separate clauses, which BSB combines.
The Hebrew includes a request particle in the order to find the arrows; BSB leaves it implicit and supplies Jonathan as the shooter where the Hebrew uses “he.”
The Hebrew says the boy reached the arrow’s place which Jonathan had shot; BSB supplies the arrow’s having fallen there.
The Hebrew calls him “Jonathan’s boy” and names plural “arrows”; BSB uses “the boy” and singular “the arrow.”
The Hebrew commands taking the equipment into the city, without a separate “back”; BSB supplies “back.”

The Hebrew says David rose from beside the south, without explicitly naming the stone here. BSB supplies “of the stone” and names Jonathan as David’s partner where the Hebrew uses reciprocal expressions.

The Hebrew’s oath says the LORD is between them; BSB supplies “a witness.” It uses the seed image for descendants, leaves David unnamed at his departure, and says Jonathan came into the city rather than explicitly went back.
